raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Stack (6/6), merge in order: [#44851](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44851) → [#44852](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44852) → [#44853](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44853) → [#44854](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44854) → [#44863](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44863) → [#44869](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44869)

## Motivation

Gemma4 on XPU launches normalization and RoPE separately for every attention layer. Shared-KV layers additionally allocate a dummy key tensor just to rotate Q. Fuse these operations while preserving the BF16/FP16 normalization rounding boundary and the existing checkpoint weights.

## Modifications

- Extend the existing Gemma QKV norm/RoPE operator to XPU and query-only shared-KV calls.
- Dispatch eligible XPU Gemma4 layers through the fused operator, including unweighted V normalization for nonshared layers.
- Match native XPU rotary contraction order. Explicitly materialize the FP16 intermediate encoding before rotation to preserve its rounding, including subnormal and nonfinite values.

## Accuracy Tests

Intel Arc Pro B70, `google/gemma-4-E2B-it`, BF16, TP1:

- Official `sgl-eval` GSM8K-200: 163/200 (81.5%), zero errors, two truncated responses. Temperature 1, top_p 0.95, seed 42, max_tokens 2048, concurrency 8, thinking disabled.
- Six greedy model parity cases matched, including 1,016- and 1,814-token prompts.
- All 64 sampled native XPU kernel comparisons matched exactly across BF16/FP16, shared/nonshared KV, geometries, and batch sizes. Graph replay, packed-stride guards, FP16 cancellation, and 8,204 FP16 rounding edge/random inputs passed.
- 123 CPU namespace/dispatch tests passed.
- All four serving capture tests passed (three-step and single-step MTP), in 88.754 seconds.

Expanded 256-token serving comparisons also expose output variation within control repeats. Of three differing prompts replayed on the same GPU/configuration with cache flushed before each repeat, two matched across all four control/candidate runs; one varied in every run. These measurements do not establish bitwise model equivalence on arbitrary prompts. CUDA execution was not available locally; its existing contraction path is preserved.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same B70, same serving configuration and unchanged BF16 weights; current stack tip as control. Captured three-step MTP, max_running_requests=32, context_length=8192, max_total_tokens=32768, page_size=64, overlap disabled. Control/candidate/candidate/control sequence, 256 output tokens, 64 requests at c1 and 128 at c8/c32. Each server switch discarded a full 128-request c32 warmup before measurement.

| Concurrency | Control mean TPOT (ms) | Candidate mean TPOT (ms) | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 4.155 | 4.116 | 0.95% |
| 8 | 6.118 | 6.049 | 1.14% |
| 32 | 11.334 | 11.102 | 2.04% |

Both candidate repeats were faster than both control repeats at every measured concurrency. The subset with identical generated text in all four runs showed streaming-interval TPOT reductions of 1.03%, 1.15%, and 1.94%, respectively. These are results on this device/workload, not a claim for all XPU hardware or batch sizes.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add kernel tests with CI registration.
- [x] Document the extended operator contract in its docstring.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed measurements.
- [x] Follow the existing kernel organization and code style.

+@triton.jit
+def _xpu_fp16_intermediate(value):
+    # An FP32 -> FP16 -> FP32 pair can be removed before an XPU FMA by the
+    # device compiler. Decode the observable FP16 bits to retain that rounding.
+    bits = value.to(tl.float16).to(tl.uint16, bitcast=True).to(tl.uint32)
+    sign = (bits & 0x8000) << 16
+    exponent = (bits >> 10) & 0x1F
+    fraction = bits & 0x3FF
+    normal = sign | ((exponent + 112) << 23) | (fraction << 13)
+    special = sign | 0x7F800000 | (fraction << 13)
+    subnormal = fraction.to(tl.float32) * (2.0**-24)
+    subnormal = (subnormal.to(tl.uint32, bitcast=True) | sign).to(
+        tl.float32, bitcast=True
+    )
+    return tl.where(
+        exponent == 0,
+        subnormal,
+        tl.where(
+            exponent == 31,
+            special.to(tl.float32, bitcast=True),
+            normal.to(tl.float32, bitcast=True),
+        ),
+    )
+

+"""Fused Gemma normalization/NeoX RoPE with packed or shared KV."""
+
+import unittest
+
+import torch
+import triton
+import triton.language as tl
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.fused_qk_rmsnorm_rope_gate import (
+    _xpu_fp16_intermediate,
+)
+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.gemma_qkv_norm_rope import gemma_qkv_norm_rope
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci, register_xpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=15, stage="base-b-kernel-unit", runner_config="1-gpu-large")
+register_xpu_ci(est_time=20, stage="stage-b", runner_config="1-gpu-xpu")
+
+DEVICE = "xpu" if torch.xpu.is_available() else "cuda"
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _round_intermediate_kernel(X, Y, N: tl.constexpr, BLOCK: tl.constexpr):
+    offsets = tl.program_id(0) * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
+    value = tl.load(X + offsets, offsets < N, other=0)
+    tl.store(Y + offsets, _xpu_fp16_intermediate(value), offsets < N)
+
+
+def reference(x, weight, dim, cache=None, positions=None):
+    dtype = x.dtype
+    x = x.reshape(x.shape[0], -1, dim).float()
+    normalized = (
+        x * torch.rsqrt(x.square().mean(-1, keepdim=True) + 1e-6) * weight
+    ).to(dtype)
+    if cache is None:
+        return normalized.flatten(1)
+    normalized = normalized.float()
+    half = cache.shape[1] // 2
+    cosine, sine = cache[positions].chunk(2, -1)
+    cosine, sine = cosine[:, None, :], sine[:, None, :]
+    first, second = normalized[..., :half], normalized[..., half : 2 * half]
+    result = torch.cat(
+        (
+            first * cosine - second * sine,
+            second * cosine + first * sine,
+            normalized[..., 2 * half :],
+        ),
+        -1,
+    )
+    return result.to(dtype).flatten(1)
+
+
+@unittest.skipUnless(
+    torch.xpu.is_available() or torch.cuda.is_available(), "requires XPU or CUDA"
+)
+class TestGemmaQKVNormRope(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_packed_strides_shared_kv_and_rounding(self):
+        torch.manual_seed(44)
+        for dim, rotary in ((128, 64), (256, 64), (256, 256), (512, 128), (512, 512)):
+            for dtype in (torch.bfloat16, torch.float16):
+                for shared in (False, True):
+                    with self.subTest(
+                        dim=dim, rotary=rotary, dtype=dtype, shared=shared
+                    ):
+                        # Include guards and a nontrivial token stride; each Q/K/V
+                        # view has contiguous heads but is not itself contiguous.
+                        storage = torch.randn(
+                            (4, 10 * dim + 16), device=DEVICE, dtype=dtype
+                        )
+                        original = storage.clone()
+                        q, k, v = storage[:, : 10 * dim].split((8 * dim, dim, dim), -1)
+                        qw, kw = torch.randn((2, dim), device=DEVICE, dtype=dtype)
+                        angles = torch.randn((256, rotary // 2), device=DEVICE)
+                        cache = torch.cat((angles.cos(), angles.sin()), -1)
+                        positions = torch.tensor(
+                            [0, 7, 127, 255], device=DEVICE, dtype=torch.int64
+                        )
+                        expected_q = reference(q, qw, dim, cache, positions)
+                        expected_k = reference(k, kw, dim, cache, positions)
+                        expected_v = reference(v, 1.0, dim)
+                        gemma_qkv_norm_rope(
+                            q,
+                            None if shared else k,
+                            None if shared else v,
+                            qw,
+                            None if shared else kw,
+                            cache,
+                            positions,
+                            8,
+                            1,
+                            dim,
+                            rotary,
+                            1e-6,
+                        )
+                        tolerance = (
+                            dict(rtol=0.015625, atol=0.0078125)
+                            if dtype == torch.bfloat16
+                            # Two rounded norm operands feed a subtract in RoPE;
+                            # cancellation needs an absolute bound of two FP16 eps.
+                            else dict(rtol=0.002, atol=2 * torch.finfo(dtype).eps)
+                        )
+                        torch.testing.assert_close(q, expected_q, **tolerance)
+                        if shared:
+                            torch.testing.assert_close(
+                                storage[:, 8 * dim :],
+                                original[:, 8 * dim :],
+                                rtol=0,
+                                atol=0,
+                            )
+                        else:
+                            torch.testing.assert_close(k, expected_k, **tolerance)
+                            torch.testing.assert_close(v, expected_v, **tolerance)
+                            torch.testing.assert_close(
+                                storage[:, 10 * dim :],
+                                original[:, 10 * dim :],
+                                rtol=0,
+                                atol=0,
+                            )
+
+    @unittest.skipUnless(torch.xpu.is_available(), "XPU rounding fence")
+    def test_fp16_rounding_fence_edges(self):
+        generator = torch.Generator().manual_seed(58)
+        # Cover all exponent ranges and explicit overflow, subnormal, tie,
+        # signed-zero and non-finite values, independently of normalization.
+        bits = torch.randint(0, 2**32, (8192,), dtype=torch.int64, generator=generator)
+        values = bits.to(torch.int32).view(torch.float32)
+        edges = torch.tensor(
+            [
+                0.0,
+                -0.0,
+                2.0**-25,
+                3 * 2.0**-25,
+                2.0**-24,
+                2.0**-14,
+                65504.0,
+                65520.0,
+                -65520.0,
+                float("inf"),
+                -float("inf"),
+                float("nan"),
+            ]
+        )
+        values = torch.cat((values, edges)).to("xpu")
+        expected = values.to(torch.float16).float()
+        actual = torch.empty_like(values)
+        _round_intermediate_kernel[(triton.cdiv(values.numel(), 256),)](
+            values, actual, values.numel(), 256
+        )
+        torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, rtol=0, atol=0, equal_nan=True)
+        zeros = expected == 0
+        torch.testing.assert_close(
+            torch.signbit(actual[zeros]), torch.signbit(expected[zeros])
+        )
+
+    @unittest.skipUnless(torch.xpu.is_available(), "native XPU reference")
+    def test_native_xpu_arithmetic_is_preserved(self):
+        from sglang.kernels.ops.layernorm.gemma4_fused_ops import gemma_qkv_rmsnorm
+        from sglang.srt.layers.rotary_embedding.base import RotaryEmbedding
+
+        torch.manual_seed(47)
+        for dtype in (torch.bfloat16, torch.float16):
+            for dim, rotary in ((256, 64), (256, 256), (512, 128), (512, 512)):
+                rope = RotaryEmbedding(dim, rotary, 8192, 10000, True, dtype)
+                rope.cos_sin_cache = rope.cos_sin_cache.to("xpu")
+                qw, kw = torch.randn((2, dim), device="xpu", dtype=dtype)
+                for batch in (1, 8, 128, 512):
+                    for shared in (False, True):
+                        with self.subTest(
+                            dtype=dtype,
+                            dim=dim,
+                            rotary=rotary,
+                            batch=batch,
+                            shared=shared,

+    def test_graph_replay_reads_updated_positions_and_inputs(self):
+        dim, rotary = 256, 64

+        weight = torch.randn(dim, device=DEVICE, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+        positions = torch.zeros(8, device=DEVICE, dtype=torch.int32)
+        angles = torch.randn((256, rotary // 2), device=DEVICE)
+        cache = torch.cat((angles.cos(), angles.sin()), -1)
+
+        def run():
+            gemma_qkv_norm_rope(
+                q, None, None, weight, None, cache, positions, 8, 1, dim, rotary, 1e-6

+        with module.graph(graph):
+            run()
+        for sign, position in ((1, 7), (-1, 127)):
+            q.copy_(initial * sign)
+            positions.fill_(position)
+            expected = reference(q, weight, dim, cache, positions)
